messages:
sre_bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike for Hydrangea Corp (VPC: hydrangea-eu, Dedicated pool: dhg-eu-west-3). p99=3.7s (SLO=1.2s), p95=1.6s. Affected endpoint: POST /v1/generate. Paging oncall @maria_oncall
maria_oncall: oncall here, joining. opening war-room.
tony_infra: looking at pool telemetry — I see a sharp increase in concurrent streams. one tenant looks noisy: tenant-742.
elaine_prod: customer (Hydrangea) already reported slow UI on their engineers' channel. Sanjay FYI, they'd like proactive updates.
sanjay_ae: pinged CSM + customer Slack. they're ready for failover but prefer we try isolation first.
maria_oncall: plan: 1) isolate tenant-742 (move to throttled class) 2) scale pool + warm-spare activation 3) if no recovery -> failover tenant to eu-west-1 warm spare 4) consider rolling fallback to v1-quantized model for tenant-742.
luke_runtime: starting tenant isolation command now: 
```
POST /internal/tenants/tenant-742/actions
{ "action": "throttle", "reason": "p99-surge-20260317" }
```
response: 202 accepted, job ev-20260317-001 created.
incidentbot: job ev-20260317-001 started on node dhg-eu-3b (op id 88a7).
tony_infra: scaling dedicated pool +3 GPUs (scale-group dhg-eu-west-3). patch applied, new instances provisioning. ETA ~90-150s.
luke_runtime: digging into KV cache metrics — tenant-742 has high cache churn and large context windows, causing KV miss storm.
katrina_support: adding notes to Hydrangea support ticket (#H-4591) and notifying their SRE alias.
elaine_prod: what's the current routing policy? can we route only tenant-742 away while leaving others?
maria_oncall: yes — roll a per-tenant routing override to divert tenant-742 to the warm spare pool once it's ready. doing that if isolation + scale fail.
incidentbot: pool scale events: scale-up started (req id s-54789-01). monitoring autoscaler logs.
tony_infra: pool nodes reporting GPU warm, registering with runtime. new capacity online in 110s.
~2 minutes later~
luke_runtime: eviction/throttle job shows reduced concurrent streams from tenant-742 by ~60%. p95 drops to 1.1s, p99 to 1.9s (partial recovery).
maria_oncall: good. keep monitoring for 5m. keep customer updated: Sanjay?
sanjay_ae: told customer we throttled noisy traffic and scaled their pool; they want metrics after stabilization. they're okay holding off failover for now.
elaine_prod: also enabling short-term model fallback for tenant-742 to v1-q to reduce per-token latency — enabling config now.
luke_runtime: model fallback applied for tenant-742 (variant v1-q). initial token latency improvement ~30%.
incidentbot: alert: p99 now 1.3s. trending down.
maria_oncall: marking mitigations: eviction + scale + quantized fallback. set follow-up: run a post-incident eval for quality regressions w/ Hydrangea prompt set. assign to research.
katrina_support: creating incident note: impact=degraded for Hydrangea workspace users, window started 2026-03-17T12:00Z, mitigation=throttle+scale+fallback. CSM looped.
tony_infra: next steps: root cause triage — KV cache pressure + oversized contexts from tenant-742. propose: implement per-tenant KV limits + burst protection, and add early detection alert for tenant-level concurrency.
maria_oncall: agreed. Sanjay, we'll schedule technical remediation with Hydrangea next week. For now, keep warm spare routing config as a runbook step.
sanjay_ae: customer accepts that plan. request SLO credit? we'll coordinate finance after postmortem.
maria_oncall: I'll hand this to L2 for post-incident work. closing war-room in 10m unless we see regression. thanks all. :thumbsup:
incidentbot: war-room closed by maria_oncall; summary posted to #incidents-log; runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/tenant-noise-isolation
katrina_support: handoff note added to ticket H-4591, assigning to support-2 for customer follow-up.
